newsitem.title: TURKEY: Eight die in Kurd guerrilla riot at Turkish jail.
newsitem.headline: Eight die in Kurd guerrilla riot at Turkish jail.

text.p: Eight people died in a riot by Kurdish rebel prisoners at a high-security Turkish jail on Tuesday before security forces brought the disturbance under control.
"We know of eight dead," a hospital source told Reuters. He said 17 people were injured in the incident at Diyarbakir jail in the mainly-Kurdish southeast of Turkey.
The ATV television station, quoting regional governor Necati Bilican, said seven inmates had died after Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels started a fire during the riot.
The channel said the militants were protesting at the government's failure to improve prison conditions following a nationwide hunger strike in July.
"The PKK staged a protest to complain that the prison's authorities had not kept the promises given in the recent hunger strike," ATV said. "The inmates started a fire."

State-run Anatolian news agency said security forces later brought both the fire and the riot under control. Police and soldiers formed a cordon around the jail and refused to let journalists near the building, witnesses said.
Twelve left-wing militant prisoners died in the hunger strike that ended after the Islamist-led government granted many of the inmates' demands for better prison conditions.
Thousands of Kurdish prisoners, many linked to the PKK, had supported the hunger strike with temporary fasts.
More than 20,000 people have died in a bitter conflict between government forces and the PKK rebels, fighting for autonomy or independence in southeast Turkey since 1984.
Security forces, including mountain commandos, pressed an air and land offensive against the guerrillas in the eastern mountains on Tuesday.
Military officials said troops backed by helicopters and the rebels were engaged in heavy fighting at several points in the rugged province of Tunceli.
Troops also launched a major attack on guerrilla positions near the remote Iraqi border.
Around 15 rebels have been killed in Tunceli in the last two days, security officials said. There was no word of military casualties.
